title: Audit ledger mutation record format and actor/subject provenance for admin operations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a single, queryable "ledger" record shape for admin-facing audit events that captures who initiated a change, what object(s) were affected, and a concise mutation encoding that allows reconstruction, intent analysis, and efficient indexing. This ticket specifies the event fields, a mutation encoding called the 'mutation array' (path/operation/before/after), SAML/SSO linkage conventions, and operational constraints (redaction, sampling, storage size). The ledger is intended to be the canonical ingest shape for audit stores, downstream analyzers, and the Console timeline UI. We must support both human admin operations (UI/CLI) and automated control-plane changes (service accounts, webhook processors, policy enforcers).

Scope: schema for admin change events (create/update/delete/attach/detach/permission-grant/revoke), examples for RBAC changes and SAML-linked session events, redaction rules for PII and credentials, indexing hints (primary query fields), and recommended retention/sampling policies. This spec intentionally avoids opaque binary diffs: we prefer a sparse, typed mutation array that expresses intent and is human-readable for debugging while remaining compact for storage.

Non‑goals: full implementation of an ingestion pipeline, migration of historical audit lines (handled in follow-up), or defining UI rendering styles beyond minimal metadata that the Console requires.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable JSON schema text describing the canonical audit ledger record is checked into the security/design Confluence page and referenced from the ingest pipeline README.
All required fields (unique id, timestamp, initiator, subject, action, mutation array, session context, request_id) appear in the schema and examples.
Three representative example events (role grant, policy update with multiple path changes, SAML login + failed assertion) are included and validated against the schema.
Redaction rules for tokens/keys/SSNs are documented and an acceptance test that redacts before persistence is defined.
Indexing recommendations (fields to index for fast queries) are documented and reviewed with storage/infra.
Security review sign-off recorded and the ticket updated with any follow-up items required by the review.
A short RFC is linked and scheduled for the platform design review meeting.
Console team receives a minimal sample JSON and confirms fields necessary for timeline rendering (human_summary, diffs_preview, severity).
tasks: Draft JSON schema for ledger record and mutation array (schema file path in Confluence).
Write three canonical examples and validate with ajv/local validator.
Define and document SAML/SSO linkage fields (assertion_id, saml_subject, idp_hint, session_index).
Propose redaction rules and a pre-commit filter function prototype for persistence layer.
Coordinate with infra to surface indexing/storage implications and cost estimate.
Get security review and update schema for any requested privacy controls.
Add ingest validation at the receiver to ensure event size limits and required fields; create follow-up ENG for implementation.
comments: 2025-02-04 | Miguel Ortega: Initial draft uploaded to Confluence; omitted fields to review: effective_permissions_snapshot vs roles_snapshot. Suggest roles_snapshot only to save storage unless policy resolution is required for debugging.

2025-02-05 | Priya Menon (Security): Please ensure SAML PII fields are redacted by default and that assertion raw payloads are never stored in plain text. We need a separate encrypted audit bucket for cases where investigators require raw assertions.
2025-02-06 | Asha Patel: Agreed with Priya. Added 'encrypted_blob_ref' optional field to schema. This stores a KMS-backed pointer when raw assertion storage is explicitly approved and audited.

2025-02-07 | Console PM (Jonah Reed): Console needs 'human_summary' and 'preview_mutations' flattened strings on the event for quick timeline view; we'll accept pagination-friendly excerpts rather than full mutation arrays on the initial UI payload.

2025-02-09 | Storage Lead (Eve Zhang): Indexing fields proposed: timestamp, initiator.id, subject.id, action, request_id, policy_version. Recommend keeping mutation array off the primary index to avoid high-cardinality penalties.
2025-02-10 | Miguel Ortega: Updated schema proposal attached in Confluence. Marking In Progress pending infra cost estimate and security sign-off.

notes_and_tradeoffs: We choose a typed mutation array instead of binary diffs to maximize human inspectability and make ad-hoc debugging easier for SREs during incidents.

Storing full 'effective_permissions' for every event increases storage but dramatically simplifies post-hoc access investigations; propose sampling full snapshots and keeping role changes dense in the mutation array.
Raw SAML assertions are sensitive. By default they are not stored; when investigators opt-in, store encrypted blobs with strict ACLs and a secondary approval workflow.
Indexing the mutation array is expensive; instead index top-level subject.id, initiator.id, action, and policy_version and provide tooling to scan mutation arrays in background jobs for deep queries.
We avoid embedding deep policy resolution results in every event by linking to a policy_version field. This allows deterministic reconstructions by combining stored policy versions and mutations.
Sampling: for high-volume service-account churn we recommend 1% sampling of full snapshots and always store mutation array entries for each operation.
Size limits: enforce 256KB event payload max at ingest. For larger events require shard to encrypted blob with reference placed in the ledger event.
Backward compatibility: ingest layer should accept older shapes and normalize them into the new ledger shape. A migration/adapter layer will be implemented in a follow-up ticket.
